label: prop:level-selection-not-linear
title: Linear level-selection is excluded (exponential beats linear)
html:
Proposition. Let w = w_{\mathrm{std}} be the branched brane-tower weight, which by prop:tower-geometric-lower-bound satisfies c\,r^{k} \leq w(k) for k \geq 3 with r = \sqrt{2} > 1 and c = 1/30 > 0. If the binding is extensive — w(A) \leq M \cdot A for every A \geq 1 — then a contradiction follows. Consequently no linear level-selection rule k(A) = A (nor bond-count k(A) = A(A-1)/2, a fortiori) is consistent with extensive binding: the selected jet level grows at most logarithmically in A.

Proof idea. The tower bound gives c\,r^{A} \leq w(A) \leq M\cdot A for all A \geq 1. But a geometric c\,r^{A} with r > 1 eventually outgrows any linear M\cdot A — formally (A) = o(r^{A}) as A \to \infty — so the inequality cannot hold for all A. Dividing the surviving bound by c and taking \log_r shows k(A) \leq \log_r\!\big((M/c)\,A\big), i.e. at most logarithmic growth.

Restriction of the hypothesis to A \geq 1. Extensivity is imposed only for A \geq 1, the physical regime. Excluding A = 0 ensures the exclusion is the genuine growth argument rather than a degenerate boundary coincidence: at A = 0 the linear side is M \cdot 0 = 0, so the inequality would fail or hold for reasons unrelated to the exponential-versus-linear mechanism.

This paragraph previously justified the restriction by saying that "the tower bound forces w(0) \geq c > 0 while M \cdot 0 = 0". That reading was backwards. The tower bound forces no such thing: w_{\mathrm{std}}(0) = 0, because no diagram of fewer than three cells contains (2,1). What the A = 0 case actually exhibited was not a nuisance of the conclusion but a falsity in the antecedent — the growth hypothesis, then stated for every k, could not hold at all. That is why prop:tower-geometric-lower-bound now carries a threshold, and why this proposition is unconditional rather than conditional.

Lean structure

QOU.Mass.LevelSelection.no_linear_selection proves the contradiction outright, sorry-free, taking the tower bound as the class hypothesis [TowerGeometricLowerBound w r c k₀]. The exponential-beats-linear step is Mathlib's isLittleO_coe_const_pow_of_one_lt ((A:\mathbb{R}) = o[\mathrm{atTop}]\, r^{A}); #print axioms reports only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound. The companion inequality linear_selection_bound (c\,r^{A} \leq M\cdot A) is the un-contradicted form; this proposition is the exclusion it entails.

The hypothesis is discharged, so the exclusion is not conditional. QOU.Mass.WStd.towerGeometricLowerBound_wStd inhabits the class at k_{0} = 3, and QOU.Mass.WStd.no_linear_selection_wStd is this theorem at the actual w_{\mathrm{std}} with no class argument to supply; no_superlinear_selection_wStd is its bond-count companion. Until that instance existed the class had none, so neither exclusion could be applied to any concrete weight. The threshold costs the argument nothing, because both proofs already select their A from an atTop filter.
